title: GitHub Actions
objectives: Understand GitHub Actions via a real-life analogy
Master workflows, jobs, steps, matrix, reusable + composite actions
Configure runners + caching + concurrency for speed

sections.markdown:
**Think of GitHub Actions as GitHub's built-in factory-line automation.**

Event (push, PR, schedule, manual, webhook) triggers a **workflow** (YAML file in `.github/workflows/`). Workflow consists of **jobs** running on **runners** (VMs — Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, or self-hosted). Each job runs a sequence of **steps** — reusable **actions** (from marketplace) or shell commands.

- **Free tier is generous** for public repos + startups.
- **Marketplace of 20K+ actions** — pre-built steps for everything (build Flutter, deploy Firebase, upload to Play).
- **Multi-OS matrix** — same workflow across Ubuntu + macOS + Windows.
- **Secrets + Environments** — safe secret injection + manual approval gates.
- **Concurrency + reusable workflows** — control cost + DRY.

**Why every Flutter team on GitHub uses Actions:** zero infra setup (no Jenkins server); tight integration with PRs + code review; huge marketplace covers Flutter, Fastlane, Firebase; free minutes for public repos + reasonable paid pricing for private. Codemagic + Bitrise offer Flutter-tuned alternatives — pick based on team preference.

**GitHub Actions** is GitHub's integrated CI/CD service. **Workflow** = YAML file describing automation. **Trigger events** — push, PR, schedule (cron), workflow_dispatch (manual), repository_dispatch (webhook). **Jobs** run in parallel by default; can depend via `needs`. **Runners** — GitHub-hosted (Ubuntu / macOS / Windows) or self-hosted. **Steps** = actions (reusable modules) or shell commands. **Secrets + Environments** — safe secret storage + protection rules.
## Anatomy of a workflow

sections.code:
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: Flutter CI            # human-readable

on:                          # triggers
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:         # manual trigger
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 3 * * *'      # nightly at 03:00 UTC

concurrency:                 # cancel prior runs on new push
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  FLUTTER_VERSION: '3.24.0'

jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: macos-14        # runner OS
    strategy:
      matrix:                # matrix of target platforms
        target: [android, ios]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          flutter-version: ${{ env.FLUTTER_VERSION }}
          cache: true         # cache Flutter SDK + pub

      - name: pub get
        run: flutter pub get

      - name: analyze
        run: flutter analyze

      - name: test
        run: flutter test --coverage

      - name: build android
        if: matrix.target == 'android'
        run: flutter build appbundle --release --obfuscate --split-debug-info=./symbols

      - name: build ios
        if: matrix.target == 'ios'
        run: flutter build ipa --release --no-codesign --obfuscate --split-debug-info=./symbols

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: bundle-${{ matrix.target }}
          path: build/**/output/*

  distribute:
    needs: ci
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: internal     # env with approvals + separate secrets
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
      - uses: wzieba/Firebase-Distribution-Github-Action@v1
        with:
          appId: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_APP_ID }}
          serviceCredentialsFileContent: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_SA_JSON }}
          groups: qa
          file: bundle-android/app-release.aab

sections.markdown: ## Reusable + composite actions

sections.code:
# .github/workflows/build-flutter.yml — REUSABLE workflow
name: Reusable Flutter Build
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      flutter-version: {type: string, required: true}
      flavor: {type: string, default: 'dev'}
    secrets:
      FIREBASE_SA_JSON: {required: true}

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: macos-14
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with: {flutter-version: ${{ inputs.flutter-version }}}
      - run: flutter build appbundle --flavor ${{ inputs.flavor }}

# Call it from another workflow:
#   uses: ./.github/workflows/build-flutter.yml
#   with: {flutter-version: '3.24.0', flavor: 'prod'}
#   secrets: {FIREBASE_SA_JSON: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_SA_JSON }}}

# ────── Composite action — a group of steps ──────
# .github/actions/setup-flutter/action.yml
name: Setup Flutter
description: 'Install Flutter + pub get + cache'
inputs:
  version: {default: '3.24.0'}
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
      with: {flutter-version: ${{ inputs.version }}, cache: true}
    - run: flutter pub get
      shell: bash

# In another workflow:
#   - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter
#     with: {version: '3.24.0'}

sections.markdown: ## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Third-party actions pinned to a tag.** `@v1` can be moved by the maintainer; a compromised action steals your secrets. Pin to a full commit SHA.
**Mistake 2: `pull_request_target` misused.** Runs with repo secrets on forked PRs; attackers exfiltrate. Restrict to specific actions.
**Mistake 3: Secrets echoed to logs.** `echo $SECRET` prints even with masking. Never echo raw secrets.
**Mistake 4: Broad `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions.** Default is read-write; set `permissions: read-all` unless job needs more.
**Mistake 5: No caching.** Every run re-downloads dependencies; 5-10 min wasted.
**Mistake 6: Sequential when parallel possible.** Android + iOS builds should run in parallel via matrix.
**Mistake 7: macOS runners for everything.** macOS costs 10× more minutes than Ubuntu; use Ubuntu for Android + tests where possible.
**Mistake 8: No concurrency control.** Old runs keep going when new push arrives; wasted minutes.
## Best practices
**1. Pin third-party actions to a SHA.**
**2. Least-privilege `permissions:`** — read-only default.
**3. Cache Flutter SDK + pub + gradle + pods.**
**4. Matrix builds** for cross-platform.
**5. `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true`** to skip stale runs.
**6. Environments with approvals for prod.**
**7. Reusable workflows + composite actions** — DRY across repos.
**8. Ubuntu > macOS > Windows** cost order — pick minimum needed.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Workflow triggering on PR that runs format + analyze + test.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — Matrix: Android + iOS build in parallel.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Cache pub / gradle / pods; measure delta.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — Reusable workflow used by 3 caller workflows.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — Environment with required reviewers for prod deploy.
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Custom composite action encapsulating Flutter setup + cache.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: Actions vs reusable workflows vs composite actions?**

**A:** **Action** — a self-contained module in the marketplace (`uses: actions/checkout@v4`). Can be JavaScript, Docker, or composite. **Reusable workflow** — a WHOLE workflow file called from another workflow via `uses: ./.github/workflows/build.yml`. Full workflow features (matrix, env, jobs). Great for cross-repo automation. **Composite action** — a group of steps packaged as an action in a directory (`.github/actions/setup-flutter/action.yml`). Can accept inputs; can use other actions. Great for local DRY. **Rule:** use marketplace actions for common tasks; composite actions to DRY steps within a repo; reusable workflows to DRY entire pipelines across teams. Interviewer bonus: knowing the trade-off.

**Q2: How do Environments work + when do you use them?**

**A:** **Environments** = named deployment targets (`internal`, `staging`, `prod`) with per-env: **(1) Secrets** — env-specific credentials (prod secrets never leak to dev pipeline). **(2) Protection rules** — required reviewers, wait timer, allowed branches (only `main` deploys to prod). **(3) Deployment history** — visible in repo UI. **(4) Environment-scoped variables** — env-specific config. **Use:** attach `environment: prod` to a job; before it runs, GitHub pauses + notifies reviewers; only proceeds after approval. **Real-world:** prod releases gated by 2 reviewers; staging auto-approves; dev unrestricted. **Combines with:** OIDC for secretless cloud auth (no static AWS keys — fetch temporary creds per run). Interviewer signal: comprehensive answer including OIDC bonus.

**Q3: How would you speed up a slow Actions pipeline?**

**A:** **Profile first** — go to Actions tab, click a run, see time-per-step. **Then:** (1) **Cache** pub / gradle / pods via `actions/cache` keyed by lockfile hash. (2) **Parallel matrix** — Android || iOS. (3) **Path filters** — skip iOS build if only android code changed. (4) **`concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true`** — avoid stale runs. (5) **Faster runner** — `macos-14` M2 chips are 2-3× faster than Intel. (6) **Reduce steps** — combine `pub get` + `dart pub upgrade` into fewer commands. (7) **Split tests** — `--concurrency N` inside `flutter test`; or shard across matrix jobs. (8) **Pre-built base images** for Linux Flutter. (9) **Self-hosted runners** at scale (macOS especially). (10) **Fail fast** — `strategy: fail-fast: true` cancels sibling matrix jobs on first failure. **Measure delta** — the savings compound across hundreds of runs/week.

**Q4: How do you keep the Actions supply chain secure?**

**A:** **(1) Pin third-party actions to a full commit SHA** — not `@v1` tags (mutable). Dependabot can bump these safely. **(2) Least-privilege `permissions:`** — start read-only; grant per-job. **(3) Restrict `GITHUB_TOKEN`** by default. **(4) OIDC for cloud auth** — no static AWS/GCP keys; fetch short-lived creds per run. **(5) `pull_request_target` cautiously** — grants secrets to forked PR code; use only for trusted actions. **(6) Review action source** before adding — some 'popular' actions have supply-chain history. **(7) Cache scoping** — a compromised cache serves malicious deps; namespace + scope. **(8) Secret scanning** on the repo. **(9) Audit workflow runs** — unusual patterns. **(10) Codeowners on `.github/`** — require review for workflow changes. **(11) Branch protection includes workflow files.** Interviewer bonus signal: comprehensive layered defense.

**Q5: When would you use self-hosted runners?**

**A:** **Reasons:** (1) **Cost** — heavy macOS build minutes get expensive on GitHub-hosted; self-hosted Mac Studio pays off at scale. (2) **Special hardware** — GPU, custom devices. (3) **Local network access** — VPN, internal services. (4) **Compliance** — regulated environments requiring on-premise. (5) **Persistent state** — pre-warmed caches, big Docker layers. **Costs:** (1) **Maintenance** — patches, updates, cleanup between runs. (2) **Security** — self-hosted runners are persistent; a compromised job can persist secrets or malicious code. (3) **Scaling** — need to manage runner pool. **Best practices:** (a) ephemeral runners (spun up per job, torn down after). (b) never expose to public PRs. (c) least-privilege network + service account. (d) monitor + patch aggressively. **GitHub's ARC (Actions Runner Controller)** for Kubernetes-managed autoscaling. Interviewer signal: knowing the trade-offs.

**Q6: How do you debug a failing workflow?**

**A:** **(1) Read the run log** — GitHub UI shows step-by-step; expand the failing step. **(2) Enable debug logging** — set repo secrets `ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG=true` + `ACTIONS_RUNNER_DEBUG=true` → verbose logs. **(3) `tmate` action** — SSH into the runner mid-workflow to poke around. **(4) Print environment** — a temporary step `env | sort` shows what's set. **(5) Re-run failed jobs** — GitHub retries individual jobs. **(6) `act` locally** — run workflows on your laptop via Docker for fast iteration. **(7) Print action versions** — `github.action_ref` + `github.workflow_ref` for reproducibility. **(8) Isolate — comment out unrelated steps to bisect. **(9) Check quota/rate limits** — 'API rate limit exceeded' happens with over-actioning. **(10) File a workflow-dispatch button** for one-off manual runs to test hypotheses. Interviewer bonus: knowing act + tmate.

## Real-world usage

- **Flutter CI/CD** — the default choice for GitHub repos.
- **Nightly + release cadence** distribution.
- **PR checks** — format + analyze + test + coverage on every PR.
- **Dependency automation** — Dependabot / Renovate.
- **Release automation** — semantic-release + auto-tag + auto-changelog.
- **NOT ideal for** — Bitbucket / GitLab (their native tools better).

## Advanced notes

- **`workflow_dispatch` inputs** — user-provided params.
- **`repository_dispatch`** — external systems trigger workflows via API.
- **`schedule`** — cron-based runs.
- **Reusable workflow `outputs:`** — pass data between workflows.
- **`actions/cache`** — key by lockfile hash.
- **OIDC** — GitHub → AWS / GCP / Vault; short-lived creds; no long-lived secrets.
- **`jobs.<id>.outputs`** — pass between jobs.
- **`if:`** conditions — branch, event, matrix values, prior step status.
- **`continue-on-error`** — don't fail whole job on this step.
- **`timeout-minutes`** — safety cap.
- **Custom action authoring** — TypeScript with `@actions/toolkit`.
- **Marketplace publishing** — versioned actions for teams.
- **`gh` CLI** — trigger workflows + query runs from terminal.
- **API** — GitHub REST + GraphQL for workflow automation.
- **Job summaries** — `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` markdown for build reports.
- **Annotations** — inline PR comments via workflow errors.
